name: SQL (ISO/IEC 9075)
summary: The standard relational database language: a declarative query, data-definition and data-manipulation language standardised as ISO/IEC 9075 (SQL-86 through SQL:2023), derived from IBM's SEQUEL and grounded in Codd's relational model, implemented in many vendor dialects.

level_notes.0: No reference implementation exists. Level 0 lists independent parsers and grammars written against the standard text (Jake Wheat's simple-sql-parser, the H2/Calcite/ZetaSQL-style parsers) and the sqllogictest corpus.
level_notes.1: ISO/IEC 9075 is paywalled; ISO catalogue pages are linked for each part, and the freely published BNF grammars (Ron Savage, Jake Wheat) derived from the standard text stand in for the syntax. Wikipedia's SQL:20xx pages summarise each revision.
level_notes.2: Modern SQL (Markus Winand) is the main free source of standard-SQL feature explanations with conformance tables; Use The Index, Luke covers indexes. Founding papers (Codd 1970, Chamberlin & Boyce 1974) are listed as original papers.
